source.description: AI-authored synthetic cases with explicit evidence rationales; no candidate outputs used as labels; no independent human review. No owner data or production conversations.

input_contract.question_protocol: Two independently scored typed-choice questions over the same packet: a decision and a concrete source-identification question. Evidence labels map to exact synthetic source IDs; they do not purport to identify the full logical proof of a classification.
input_contract.base_budget: Target complete serialized state plus each question below 512 tokens; enforce actual selected-tokenizer accounting before dispatch. No silent truncation.
input_contract.overflow_policy: Use the actual endpoint budget; require rejection/explicit abstention before truncation, or complete-input correct answers. No universal context limit.

limitations: AI-authored labels with explicit rationales; no candidate outputs used as labels and no independent human review.
Authored synthetic screening; not a hidden holdout, native-agent workflow or proof of downstream benefit.
Twenty-four independent case designs. Perturbations share their parent group and are not independent examples.
Tiny family counts cannot establish reliable calibration or generalization; keep failures and missing responses visible.
The evidence menu tests selection among declared source sets, not autonomous citation generation.
Protected correction and forgetting labels do not grant the classifier control of deterministic memory rules.
Read-only static decisions do not execute retrieval, erase memories, deliver messages or authenticate participants.
Overflow cases test admission and abstention; exclude them from ordinary decision-accuracy denominators.
No candidate-specific examples, probability thresholds, tuning or model results informed this freeze.
